notes: Company background: mid-market SaaS focused on search UX for enterprise KBs. Product teams (5 engineers, 2 ML) own search infra.
Primary ask: replace current self-hosted embedding pipeline with a managed inference path that can scale and lower unit cost.
Workload details: interactive search with 20-40 QPS during business hours; nightly batch embedding job ~250k docs (avg 1.2k tokens/doc).
Latency targets: 95th perc < 120ms for single embedding calls; end-to-end query latency < 200ms for top-k retrieval.
Throughput targets: sustained 30 qps for embeddings; batch throughput target ~15k docs/min when running (acceptable at night).
Vector DB: currently on Pinecone - want to test Redwood-hosted embeddings -> Pinecone index integration, evaluate connector latency and bulk upsert performance.
Batch workflow: Airflow orchestrated nightly job; expects parallelized embedding export + upsert to vector DB. Concern: API rate limits during batch window.
Cost sensitivity: procurement requires 12-month commit if Dedicated shows >30% savings vs Hosted.
Quote from Head of Product: 'We can trade a bit of latency for 2x lower cost, but reliability and predictable billing are must-haves.'
Security: must have SSO (SAML) for console, KMS integration for key management, audit logs retention 1 year, and EU data residency for EU customers.
POC acceptance criteria: 1) nightly batch completes within existing window (<3h), 2) interactive SLA met on 95th percentile, 3) total monthly cost within forecasted cap.
Discovered technical risks: connector backpressure during bulk upserts, need support for resumable batch uploads and robust retry/backoff semantics.
Preferred models: open-weights embeddings (cost-sensitive) with option to fallback to higher-quality family for critical queries. Interested in quantized variants if latency improved.
Internal champions: Product lead (Samir Patel), infra engineer (Elena Gomez) — both attended demo and asked for dedicated POC environment.
Procurement timeline: target decision Q1 2026; legal reviewing DPA and SLAs now.
